record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Equations of motion in a rarefied medium
record.original_question: For a body moving freely in a rarefied medium in R^n, n ≥ 1, within the framework of Newtonian aerodynamics, determine the correct dynamical equation or equations of motion and prove an existence-and-uniqueness theorem for the resulting evolution.

evidence.quote: Problem: Determine the equation(s) of dynamics and prove a/the theorem of existence and uniqueness.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a body moving freely (subject to no external forces other than collisions with medium particles) through a rarefied medium in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 1$, modeled within the framework of Newtonian aerodynamics. In this model, the medium consists of point particles of negligible size, initially at rest (or distributed according to a prescribed velocity distribution), which do not interact with each other and which collide elastically with the boundary of the body. The body is a bounded connected domain with sufficiently regular (e.g. piecewise smooth) boundary, of finite mass and moment of inertia, and its configuration at time $t$ is described by its center of mass position, its orientation (an element of $SO(n)$), and the corresponding linear and angular velocities. The force and torque exerted on the body at each instant are obtained by integrating the momentum transfer from elastic collisions of medium particles with the body's boundary, taking into account that incoming particles are screened by the body itself.

Problem: Formulate the correct system of dynamical equations governing the evolution of the body's position, orientation, linear velocity, and angular velocity in this Newtonian-aerodynamics setting, and prove a theorem of existence and uniqueness for solutions of this system, given suitable initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: Equations of motion have been derived in special cases (e.g., rough discs in the plane, spinning discs, pendulum in a rarefied flow by Plakhov and collaborators), but a general formulation with a complete existence-and-uniqueness theorem for arbitrary bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ within Newtonian aerodynamics does not appear in the literature, and the problem is posed as open in surveys of billiards/geometric optics.

status_evidence.title: Motion of a Rough Disc in Newtonian Aerodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Equations of motion of a rough disc on the plane are derived, depending on the shape of the infinitesimal boundary curve.
status_evidence.claim: Only special-case equations of motion (rough disc in the plane) are established, not a general framework.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of a Pendulum in a Rarefied Flow
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the dynamics of a specific pendulum body in a Newtonian rarefied flow.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address only specific bodies, indicating the general dynamical problem remains open.
